entries.text: The queen's childhood was pawned seven years ago and is no longer in one place or in the palace's keeping.
entries.evidence: The queen's childhood was pawned. Years ago. It is no longer in one place, and it is no longer in the palace's keeping.

entries.text: The crown's Keeper of Debts has been scrubbing the memory-debt records, erasing some entries and breaking others into traded pieces.
entries.evidence: The crown's own Keeper of Debts has been scrubbing the records. Some entries are gone entirely. Others are broken into pieces, traded like coin, diluted with each transfer.

entries.text: The largest fragment of the queen's childhood is held in the Keeper of Debts' own vault under a false name.
entries.evidence: the largest fragment is still in the Keeper's own vault, under a name that doesn't match the queen's.

entries.text: The first fragment, a summer afternoon in the palace gardens at age four, is held by the daughter of Merchant-Prince Voss in the Jade District.
entries.evidence: The daughter of Merchant-Prince Voss holds the first fragment: a summer afternoon in the palace gardens, age four.

entries.text: The second fragment is held by the memory-broker who handled the original transaction, operating from the Low Markets in the Silk District.
entries.evidence: the woman who holds the second piece is the very broker who brokered the first.

entries.text: The crown offers the Pawnbroker a single month of the recovered years as their share, entered under the shop's name.
entries.evidence: The crown is prepared to allow you a share of the retrieval. A single month from the recovered years, entered into your ledger under the shop's name.

entries.text: The original pawn ticket is in the Keeper of Debts' private vault.

entries.text: The queen's agent arrives at the pawnbroker's shop in the rain, carrying a sealed writ and a purse too light for the errand; memory-lamps gutter outside and a debt collector calls in someone's childhood down the street.
entries.evidence: The bell over the shop door rings once, and the Pawnbroker looks up from the ledger without hurry.

entries.text: The queen's childhood was pawned seven years ago and scattered; the Keeper of Debts has been scrubbing the ledger, and the largest fragment sits in the Keeper's own vault under a false name.
entries.evidence: The crown's own Keeper of Debts has been scrubbing the records. Some entries are gone entirely.

entries.text: The agent let slip that the seven years were the price of a father's salvation and a daughter's silence, then smoothed her expression.
entries.evidence: That was the price of a father's salvation, and a daughter's silence.

entries.text: The Pawnbroker demands a share of the memory for the shop's collection; the agent counters with a single month as her final offer and presses the Pawnbroker to prove their worth.
entries.evidence: A month is an insult. Show me the original pawn ticket, or tell me which district's ledger I should start with.

entries.text: Three fragments are named: the Voss daughter's garden afternoon (Jade District), the memory-broker's piece (Low Markets, Silk District), and the largest fragment in the crown's Debt Hall.
entries.evidence: Start here. The daughter of Merchant-Prince Voss holds the first fragment: a summer afternoon in the palace gardens, age four.

entries.text: The Pawnbroker's shop holds shelves of stoppered years tagged in their own handwriting.
entries.evidence: the shelves of stoppered years, the tags in your own handwriting

entries.text: The queen's childhood was pawned as the price of a father's salvation and a daughter's silence.

entries.evidence: Mira Vane, the broker there, has handled more pawned childhoods than most citizens have had years of their own.

entries.text: The crown offers to erase all of the Pawnbroker's debts — public, private, and secret — as the true payment for the commission.
entries.evidence: your name will be stricken from every ledger-house in this city. Your debts—public, private, and secret—will be erased.

entries.text: The crown's true payment is erasure of the Pawnbroker's debts — public, private, and secret — leaving them with a clean slate.
entries.evidence: your name will be stricken from every ledger-house in this city. Your debts—public, private, and secret—will be erased.

entries.text: The agent warns that some fragment-holders would rather the queen forget entirely, and calls the task an unmaking, not merely a collection.
entries.evidence: It is not merely a collection. It is an unmaking.

entries.text: Rain drums against the shop shutters and the city's memory-lamps gutter outside the pawnshop as the agent makes her offer.
entries.evidence: Outside, rain drums against the shop shutters, and the memory-lamps along the street flicker.

arcs.text: The Pawnbroker must decide whether to accept the queen's commission and on what terms, with the agent pressing for proof of worth.
The Keeper of Debts is scrubbing the crown's memory-debt ledgers and holds the largest fragment under a false name — the Pawnbroker may need to confront her.
The original pawn ticket sits in the Keeper's private vault, the only proof of the true transaction.
The agent's slip about "a father's salvation and a daughter's silence" hints at the true reason the childhood was pawned.
The Pawnbroker must decide whether to accept the crown's offer of debt-erasure as payment, or press for a higher price before committing.
The Pawnbroker must approach Mira Vane in the Silk District's Low Markets, a broker who knows the shape of the debt and will not give names freely.
The Pawnbroker must trade with the daughter of Merchant-Prince Voss in the Jade District for the first fragment, who values rarity over coin.
